correctness.rationale: The exact inverse-DFT autocorrelation identity identifies two distinct cross-correlations in odd dimension. Their common geometric-mask ratio gives the ordinary support-index sum. Invertibility of 2 modulo odd n and the observed lag determine the unordered support. Two zero-lag equations have distinct positive mask coefficients and give individual magnitudes; the cross term fixes relative phase. Separate arguments treat zero and one-sparse signals, the lower bound for one arbitrary mask and an exact antipodal real-mask obstruction in every even dimension. The attached finite checker passed 2,866 direct tests and 905 support signatures but is supplementary, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The newly proved item is the uniform two-pattern positive real bounded-contrast cyclic Fourier intensity identification theorem for all complex at-most-two-sparse inputs at every odd order, with exact decoder and sharp minimum pattern number. Full-text reading of the closest contemporary coded-diffraction, masked phase retrieval, oversampled deterministic, sparse unmasked, and designed aperture sources did not show a theorem implying it. The known even-order real-mask obstruction is not asserted as novel. One potentially close older full text could not be obtained, hence residual originality risk remains; searches are not a proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The exact worst-case minimum number of complete coded Fourier patterns for all complex two-sparse signals is a natural nontrivial sparsity-specific acquisition question. Two deterministic, experimentally attenuating rather than amplifying masks with arbitrary prescribed positive contrast suffice in each odd dimension, with direct low-cost reconstruction and a tight lower bound. This distinguishes universal sparse identifiability from high-probability or generic full-signal results and isolates a real-mask parity boundary. No unsupported claim about noisy stability or higher sparsity is made.
